original_text:
Fluid Mosaic Model
Plasma membrane is dynamic
Known as a fluid mosaic: phospholipid bilayer behaves like a fluid more than it behaves like a solid
Membrane lipids and proteins can move laterally within the bilayer
Thus the pattern (mosaic) of lipids and proteins in the cell membrane constantly changes
explanation: The Fluid Mosaic Model describes the dynamic nature of the plasma membrane. Under this model, the phospholipid bilayer behaves more like a fluid than a solid. Both lipids and membrane proteins are capable of moving laterally within the bilayer. As a result, the overall pattern or 'mosaic' of lipids and proteins in the cell membrane is constantly shifting and changing.

questions.q: Why is the cell membrane described as a 'fluid mosaic'?
opts: The membrane is completely solid but has a pattern of proteins.
The phospholipid bilayer behaves more like a fluid than a solid, and lipids and proteins can move laterally within it.
Water flows freely across the membrane in a mosaic pattern.
The membrane contains liquid-filled compartments called vesicles.
questions.exp: The fluid mosaic model describes the membrane because the phospholipid bilayer behaves like a fluid and its lipids and proteins can move laterally, changing the pattern.
